analysis.investment_thesis: Amber Enterprises dominates India's AC ODM/OEM supply chain — virtually every major brand sources components from them — but 5.26% operating margins, ROIC of ~13%, and a P/E of 120x represent the worst Magic Formula combination possible: a commodity-margin contract manufacturer priced like a premium technology compounder. Both criteria fail by wide margins.
key_strengths: 27.9% revenue CAGR over 9 years and revenues crossing INR 10,000 Cr — commanding scale in India's rapidly growing AC market with near-captive OEM relationships
100% OCF positivity (5/5 years); OCF surged to INR 711 Cr in FY25 reflecting working capital discipline at scale
Expanding into adjacencies (railway AC, defense, refrigerator liners, EV components) that carry higher margins and reduce dependence on residential RAC seasonality
key_risks: Operating margin of just 5.26% — Greenblatt requires high-ROIC businesses, and you cannot earn 25%+ ROIC from 5% margins regardless of asset turns; ROIC is only ~13%
Debt nearly tripled in 3 years (INR 1,069 Cr in FY22 → INR 2,059 Cr in FY25) while finance costs reached INR 209 Cr — leverage is rising faster than earnings quality
P/E of 120x (forward 53.58x) prices in substantial margin expansion that has not materialized; net margin remains ~2.5% — classic growth trap if margins disappoint
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~2.5% (EBIT INR 736 Cr / EV ~INR 29,400 Cr) at 37x EV/EBITDA — requires an 80% price correction to reach Magic Formula minimum thresholds
ROIC of ~13% on a 5.26% operating margin business — no pricing power evidence; margins have barely moved despite 9 years of scale-building
Finance costs of INR 209 Cr growing at 16.5% CAGR — cost of debt growing faster than operating margins can absorb; EPS quality is deteriorating
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Amber's strategic position is genuinely interesting: they manufacture for LG, Daikin, Voltas, Blue Star and others, and India's long-term AC penetration story (currently ~10% of households vs 90%+ in comparable Asian economies) provides a long runway of volume growth. The investments in railway AC, defense, and EV thermal management are smart moves toward higher-margin product categories. Management has executed well on growth — INR 1,089 Cr to INR 9,973 Cr in revenue over 9 years is remarkable.

But scale without pricing power is a treadmill. Nine years of 28% revenue CAGR has delivered operating margins that hover between 5-8% — barely above commodity-manufacturing territory. The Magic Formula identifies businesses with pricing power through sustained high ROIC; Amber's ROIC of 13% tells you definitively that this is a volume game, not a value game. At 120x trailing P/E, investors are paying a software multiple for a contract manufacturer. Debt has tripled, finance costs now consume INR 209 Cr annually against INR 251 Cr net profit — that is an 83% interest-to-profit ratio that leaves almost no buffer for execution missteps. This is the clearest AVOID in the group.
